body:
We have "Appendix W: LLM Security"

It rises a question - for whom it is and why it exists (what value it brings)?

Not all the requirements are for applications, some are for humans? W.2.1, W.2.3?

As it stands, I doubt it brings extra value for ASVS audience.

If there is a need for it to stay, it should contain only requirements and for application, also, we have removed CWE columns and made Level column to numeric.

comments.body:
If you wish to drop it, go ahead and remove it. At the very least I'd remove the link to https://github.com/OWASP/www-project-llm-verification-standard since it's mostly a dead project.

If we wish to keep this I would suggest requirements on Natural Language validation, Prompt injection, LLM access control and model training security. These are all vastly different techniques than we see in other ASVS requirements for non-AI systems.

Yes, LLM (and generative models in general, and possibly ML models in general) are quite specific and would be better served in a separate document/project. (I am aware that the same could be said of other topics we *have* included in this version of ASVS 😄.)

I think that more content would probably be needed if we really wanted to cover this topic.

(And W.3.1 and W.3.2 are quite questionnable. All the ChatGPT-clones out there are available to some extent without authentication.)
Agreed @randomstuff and @elarlang - I'm inclined to drop it and move on so this does not delay RC1.

I don't want to completely delete it but i suggest we move it out of the main folder and into an "other" folder so that people can find it if they want to reference it but it does not get included in the actual standard

Just to be clear, I don't say that ASVS must not have anything on the topic, just as it stands at the moment it rises those question I asked.

> I don't want to completely delete it but i suggest we move it out of the main folder and into an "other" folder so that people can find it if they want to reference it but it does not get included in the actual standard

I don't find this usable either. Is it fully in or fully out. We don't need to collect "maybe we need it later" trash to some corner.

As is - its fairly weak. Defenses against advisarial AI attacks have evolved quite a bit in the last year. Even major services like OpenAI had SSRF last week. Bypassing access control and content filters is trivial against most AI systems to date.

Unless we want to put serious work into this I suggest we remove it.

There are several other OWASP projects that cover AI defense a lot better than we can right now.
Removed via #2794 and I added a comment [here as well](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1730#issuecomment-2757836396) where the original addition was discussed.
